Rashi on Ketubot 14a:10:2.english: Who is the widow of [a family of] mixed lineage - About whom they testified that she is fit [to marry a priest].

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:10:3.hebrew: כל שאין - בעירובי ספקותיה לא ספק ממזרות, ולא ספק נתינות, ולא ספק עבדי מלכים, אלא ספק חלל לבדו. מש"ה נקט עבדי מלכים, משום עבדי שלמה שהיו עשירים ובעלי זרוע ונשאו להם בנות ישראל, וכגון זרעו של הורדוס, שהי' עבד לבית חשמונאי וגברה ידו ומלך:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:10:3.english: Any [family] that does not have - in the mixture of its uncertainties neither uncertainty of mamzer status, nor uncertainty of Gibeonite [netin] status, nor uncertainty of [descent from] slaves of kings, but rather uncertainty of chalal [disqualified priest] status alone. For this reason it stated "slaves of kings": because of the slaves of Solomon, who were wealthy and powerful and married daughters of Israel; and such as the descendants of Herod, who was a slave of the Hasmonean house, and his hand prevailed and he became king.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:1:1.english: Yes, from me - True, [the child] is from me.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:2:1.english: And in this [case], when he does not admit, etc. - Since you said "and furthermore" [implying that Rabban Gamliel deems the child fit even without his admission].

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:2:2.hebrew: ארוסה, הכל פסולין אצלה חוץ מן הארוס:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:2:2.english: [Regarding] a betrothed woman, all [men] are unfit for her except for the betrothed [husband].

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:3:1.hebrew: הא לכתחלה - אם בא כהן לימלך לבית דין, לא שרינן ליה לכונסה אא"כ היו רוב כשרים אצלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:3:1.english: This [is] ab initio - If a kohen comes to consult the court, we do not permit him to marry her unless a majority of [men] with her were of unflawed lineage.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:3:2.hebrew: דיעבד - אם נשאה כהן ולא נמלך, לא מפקינן לה מיניה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:3:2.english: After the fact - If a kohen married her and did not consult [a sage], we do not remove her from him.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:3:3.hebrew: והא נמי כדיעבד דמי - שנתעברה ואתה בא לפסול העובר ולאוסרה על הארוס, דאם אין אתה מאמינה, הרי אתה מוציאה מבעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:3:3.english: And this too is like [a case] after the fact - For she has become pregnant, and you are coming to disqualify the fetus and to forbid her to the betrothed [husband]; for if you do not believe her, behold, you are removing her from her husband.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:4:1.english: Did Rabbi Yehoshua say she is not believed - Evidently, we do not establish her upon [her] presumptive status.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:4:3.hebrew: על אלמנת עיסה - שהיא באה מכח ספק חלל כדלקמן, שנטמע בה ספק חלל, כגון שזרק בעל אמו הראשון לה גט ספק קרוב לו ספק קרוב לה, ומת, ונמצאת זו ספק גרושה ספק אלמנה, ונשאה כהן והוליד ממנה בן — זהו ספק חלל — והעיד ר"י על אלמנתו של זה שהיא כשרה. אלמא מוקמינן לה אחזקה, ואמרינן: אל תפסילנה לזו מספק, כלומ' שמא בעלה חלל היה:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:4:3.english: Concerning the widow of an issa - For she comes by virtue of a doubtful chalal [a disqualified priest], as [explained] below, in that a doubtful chalal was assimilated into [that family] — for example, where his mother's first husband threw her a bill of divorce [and it was] uncertain [whether it landed] closer to him or closer to her, and he died, so that she was found to be a doubtful divorcee [and] a doubtful widow; and a priest married her and fathered a son from her — this [son] is a doubtful chalal — and Rabbi Yehoshua testified concerning this [son's] widow that she is fit [for the priesthood]. Thus, we establish her upon her presumptive status [of fitness], and we say: Do not disqualify her out of doubt, meaning, [on the grounds that] perhaps her husband was a chalal.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:5:1.hebrew: בודקת וניסת - וי"ל שבדקה אחר אותן גירושין, והוגד לה שקרוב לו היו, ולא נתגרשה כלל ואלמנה היתה, וכשרה לכהן:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:5:1.english: Investigates and marries - And one can say that she investigated regarding that divorce, and she was told that [the bill of divorce] was [thrown] closer to him, and [thus she] was not divorced at all and was a widow, and is fit [to marry] a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:5:2.english: Investigates and engages in licentious intercourse - [This is said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:1.hebrew: דרבן גמליאל אדרבן גמליאל לא קשיא - בתמיה, דלא חיישת לתרוצינהו:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:1.english: [That] of Rabban Gamliel [against that] of Rabban Gamliel [is] not difficult - [Said] in astonishment: that you did not concern yourself to reconcile them.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:2.english: But isn't it taught in the latter clause - Of that [mishnah]: "He said to them, etc."

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:3.english: We have accepted your testimony - You are trustworthy to us that this is what you heard.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:4.hebrew: על כך - להתירה לכהונה, דודאי אסורה, שהכהנים שומעין לכם אם תאמרו "אסורה":
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:4.english: For this - To permit her to [marry into] the priesthood; for she is certainly forbidden, since the priests obey you if you say, "[She is] forbidden."

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:6:5.english: But not to bring near - If you say [she is] permitted.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:7:1.hebrew: התם ברי - מתניתין, היא אומרת: "ברי לי שלכשר נבעלתי":
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:7:1.english: There, [it is] certain - [In] our Mishnah, she says: "I am certain that I engaged in intercourse with an eligible [man]."

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:7:2.hebrew: הכא - גבי אלמנת עיסה, כי היכי דלדידן מספקא לן, לדידה נמי מספקא לה, וליכא למימר בה "ברי ושמא, ברי עדיף":
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:7:2.english: Here - regarding a widow of a mixed-lineage family [almanat issah], just as it is uncertain to us, it is also uncertain to her, and one cannot say regarding her, "a certain [claim] and an uncertain [claim] — the certain [claim] is superior."

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:8:1.hebrew: חד ספיקא - מתניתין חד ספיקא היא: ספק נבעלה לכשר, ספק נבעלה לפסול, שהרי לא בא זה לפנינו, ואילו בא, שמא היינו מכירים בו שהוא פסול:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:8:1.english: One uncertainty - Our Mishnah is [a case of] one uncertainty: [there is an] uncertainty [whether] she engaged in intercourse with a fit [man], [or an] uncertainty [whether] she engaged in intercourse with an unfit [man], for this [man] did not come before us, and if he had come, perhaps we would have recognized in him that he is unfit.

Rashi on Ketubot 14a:8:2.hebrew: תרי ספיקי - אמו של ספק חלל זה, בה נולד הספק, והיא עצמה לא נאסרה אלא מספק; וזו שבאה מחמת בנה, קרי לה ספק ספיקא. ומדברי רבי יוסף טוב עלם מצאתי: [אלמנת עיסה] — אשה שהיה בעלה ספק ספיקא, כגון שנתגרשה אמו מבעלה הראשון, ספק קרוב לו ספק קרוב לה, ומת בתוך שלשה חדשים, ונשאת לכהן תוך שלשה חדשים, וילדה את זה: ספק שהוא בן תשעה לראשון וכשר — ואפילו היתה מגורשת, שהרי קודם לגט נתעברה, או אפילו אחר הגט, והוא ישראל ולא כהן — וספק בן שבעה לאחרון, ובנו של כהן הוא, והרי הוא ספק חלל. הרי ספק ספיקא: שמא אינו בנו של כהן, ואת"ל בנו הוא, שמא לא היתה אמו גרושה אלא אלמנה. ולהכי קרי לה עיסה, שיש בה עירובי ספיקות הרבה, כעיסה זו שהיא בלוסה. והא דאמרינן לקמן: "כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל", היינו פירושה: כל שנטמעו בה ספק עירובי חלל:
Rashi on Ketubot 14a:8:2.english: Two uncertainties - The mother of this uncertain ḥalal — the uncertainty originated with her, and she herself was only forbidden out of [a single] uncertainty; and [as for] this [woman] who comes [into question] on account of her son, [the Gemara] calls it a double uncertainty. And from the words of Rabbi Yosef Tov Elem I found: [The widow of an isah] — a woman whose husband was a double uncertainty. For example, where his mother was divorced by her first husband — [with] an uncertainty [whether the bill of divorce was thrown] closer to him or closer to her — and [the first husband] died within three months, and she married a priest within three months, and she gave birth to this [son]: [there is] an uncertainty whether he is a nine-month [child] of the first [husband] and [therefore] fit — even if she was divorced, since she conceived before the bill of divorce, or even [if she conceived] after the bill of divorce, for he is an Israelite and not a priest — or an uncertainty whether he is a seven-month [child] of the latter [husband], and he is the son of a priest, so behold, he is an uncertain ḥalal. Behold, [here is] a double uncertainty: perhaps he is not the son of the priest; and if you should say he is his son, perhaps his mother was not a divorcée, but rather a widow. And for this reason it is called an isah [dough], because there are many mixtures of uncertainties in it, like this dough which is kneaded together. And that which we say later, "any [family] into which an uncertain ḥalal has been assimilated," this is its explanation: any [family] into which uncertain mixtures of a ḥalal have been assimilated.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:10:1.hebrew: תנו רבנן איזו היא אלמנת עיסה - קשה לרבינו תם על גרסת הספרים דגרסי אלמנת עיסה, דאם כן אית ליה לרבי יוסי דאלמנת עיסה כשרה, דהא מכשר לקמן שתוק ממזר, וכל שכן דמכשר באלמנת עיסה, כדמוכח הסוגיא. ובפרק עשרה יוחסין (ג"ז שם) אמר בהדיא דלרבי יוסי אלמנת עיסה פסולה! לכך מוחק רבינו תם "אלמנת", וגריס "איזוהי עיסה", ולענין בת קתני. וקאי אהאי דתנא בשילהי עדיות: "העיסה נאמנת לטהר ולטמא, לרחק ולקרב, לאסור ולהתיר". וה"פ: נאמנת לטהר עצמה בצויחה או בשתיקה, למר כדאית ליה ולמר כדאית ליה. לטמא ולטהר שייך לענין ממזרות ונתינות, כדתנן (קדושין דף עב:): "ממזרים ונתינים עתידין ליטהר". לרחק ולקרב שייך אחללות, כדתנן: "הכהנים שומעים לכם לרחק ולא לקרב", וכן לקמן (כתובות דף כז.): "וריחקום בני משפחה". ולאסור ולהתיר שייך אעבדים. והא דפריך בפ"ב (לקמן כתובות דף כח:): "טמאה וטהורה ס"ד?" — התם דכייל כל פסולי בחד לישנא, הוה ליה למיתני "משפחה זו כשרה וזו פסולה"; אבל אממזרות ונתינות לחודא שייך שפיר לשון טומאה וטהרה. ונאמנת נקט משום "לטהר, לקרב, ולהתיר", אף על גב דלטמא ולרחק ולאסור בצויחה או בשתיקה לא שייך נאמנות. ועלה קתני בברייתא דהכא: "איזו היא עיסה שנאמנת בצויחה או בשתיקה לטהר את הבת? כל שאין בה כו'". והכי משמע בתוספתא, דקתני: "נאמנת עיסה לטהר ולטמא, לאסור ולהתיר, לרחק ולקרב", ובאלמנת עיסה לא נגעו. והשתא לא קשה דרבי יוסי אדרבי יוסי: דהא דאכשר רבי יוסי בשתוק ממזר — אגוף העיסה קאי, להכשיר את הבת; אבל במקום שמזכיר "אלמנת עיסה" — להכשיר דוקא אלמנה ולא הבת, כדמוכח בקדושין (דף עה.), ושם ודאי פוסל רבי יוסי אפילו את האלמנה, כדמוכח נמי בקדושין. וכדברי ר"ת משמע בירושלמי, דקתני: "איזהו עיסה? כל שאין בה לא ממזר ולא נתין ולא עבדי מלכים. רבי מאיר אומר: כל שאין בה אחד מכל אלו — בתה כשרה". אלמא דבכשרות דבת מיירי ולא באלמנה. ומיהו קשה לרשב"א: כיון דהך ברייתא קיימא לפרושי ההיא דסוף עדיות, אם כן רבי מאיר דסבר דחלל בין צווח בין שתק כשר, א"כ היכי מפרש הא דקתני "לרחק"? ואור"י: הא דמכשר ר"מ חלל שותק, הני מילי כשאחרי כן שואלין ממנו אם הוא חלל אם לאו, וצווח; אבל אם לעולם שותק, פשיטא דפסול. והא דקתני דנאמנת לרחק — אם לעולם שותק:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:10:1.english: The Rabbis taught: Who is the widow of an issa [a family of questionable lineage] - Rabbeinu Tam finds difficulty with the version in the texts that reads "widow of an issa," for if so, Rabbi Yose would hold that the widow of an issa is fit [to marry a priest], since below he deems a mamzer [who is challenged and] remains silent to be fit, and all the more so does he deem fit the widow of an issa, as the sugya demonstrates. Yet in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (also there [in Kiddushin]), it states explicitly that according to Rabbi Yose, the widow of an issa is unfit! Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam deletes [the word] "widow of" and reads "Who is an issa," and it is taught with regard to [the fitness of] a daughter [born to that family]. And it refers to that which is taught at the end of Eduyot: "The issa is believed to declare pure and to declare impure, to distance and to bring near, to forbid and to permit." And this is its explanation: It is believed to declare itself pure through protesting or through silence, each [Tanna] according to his own view. "To declare impure and to declare pure" pertains to mamzer status and natin [Gibeonite] status, as we learned in a Mishnah (Kiddushin 72b): "Mamzerim and netinim will in the future be purified." "To distance and to bring near" pertains to chalal status, as we learned in a Mishnah: "The priests listen to you to distance, but not to bring near," and similarly below (Ketubot 27a): "and the members of the family distanced them." And "to forbid and to permit" pertains to slaves. And as for that which [the Gemara] asks in the second chapter (below, Ketubot 28b): "Could it enter your mind [to say] 'impure and pure'?" — there, because it grouped all disqualified lineages in one expression, it should have taught "this family is fit and that one is unfit"; however, regarding mamzer status and natin status alone, the terminology of impurity and purity is quite appropriate. And it used the term "is believed" because of "to declare pure, to bring near, and to permit," even though with respect to "to declare impure, to distance, and to forbid" through protest or silence, believability does not apply. And regarding that [Mishnah in Eduyot], the Baraita here teaches: "Who is an issa that is believed through protest or silence to declare the daughter pure? Any [family] in which there is not, etc." And this is also implied in the Tosefta, which teaches: "An issa is believed to declare pure and to declare impure, to forbid and to permit, to distance and to bring near," and they did not mention "the widow of an issa" at all. And now there is no contradiction between [one statement of] Rabbi Yose and [another statement of] Rabbi Yose: for that which Rabbi Yose declared fit in the case of a mamzer [who is challenged and] remains silent refers to the issa itself, to declare the daughter fit; whereas in a place where it mentions "widow of an issa" — [that is] to declare fit specifically the widow and not the daughter, as is proven in Kiddushin (75a), and there Rabbi Yose certainly disqualifies even the widow, as is also proven in Kiddushin. And in accordance with the words of Rabbeinu Tam, it is implied in the Yerushalmi, which teaches: "What is an issa? Any [family] in which there is neither a mamzer, nor a natin, nor slaves of kings. Rabbi Meir says: Any [family] in which there is none of all these — its daughter is fit." Thus we see that it deals with the fitness of the daughter and not with the widow. However, Rashba finds a difficulty: since this Baraita comes to explain that [Mishnah] at the end of Eduyot, if so, Rabbi Meir — who holds that a chalal is fit whether he protests or remains silent — if so, how does he explain that which it teaches, "to distance"? And Rabbi Yitzchak [Ri] says: That which Rabbi Meir deems fit a chalal who is silent applies specifically when afterward they ask him whether he is a chalal or not, and he protests; but if he remains silent forever, it is obvious that he is unfit. And that which it teaches that [the issa] is believed "to distance" — [that is] if he remains silent forever.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:1:1.hebrew: חדא דקא מודה - וללישנא קמא דיבמות, דלא דיימא מעלמא; ולאיכא דאמרי, דאפילו דיימא מעלמא, כיון דקא מודה — בתריה דידיה שדינן ליה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:1:1.english: First, he concedes - And according to the first version in Yevamot, [our case is one] where she is not rumored [to have consorted] with others; and according to [the version of] "there are those who say," even if she is rumored [to have consorted] with others, since he concedes, we attribute [the child] to him.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:1:2.hebrew: חדא דקא מודה - מצינן לפרש דאיירי לענין לאוסרה על הארוס, וה"פ: "חדא דקא מודה", הלכך אינה נאסרת עליו; "ועוד הא רב יהודה כו'" — לא קאמר "ועוד אפילו לא מודה", דאם אינו מודה פשיטא דנאסרת עליו, אלא כלומר: אפילו כי ליכא טעמא דמודה — כגון לאביי דס"פ אלמנה, מדאפקרה נפשה לגבי ארוס מפקרה נפשה נמי לגבי עלמא — אפ"ה אינה נאסרת עליו משום דנאמנת כר"ג. כן פי' לנו ר"י. ואי אפשר להעמידה, דלפי דבריו אם כן הא דאמר אביי "מדאפקרה נפשה", היינו בשלא בדקו את אמו; וזה אינו, דהא אפלוגתא דרב ושמואל קאי, דמוקמי בקדושין: מאי "שתוקי"? "בדוקי". ולמאי דגרסינן בקדושין "ארוסה שעיברה", לא קשה מידי. על כן צריך לפרש דהכא לא איירי לאוסרה עליו, אלא לענין להכשיר את הולד. והשתא הוי "ועוד" כפשוטו: ועוד דאפילו לא יודה — ולאו דקאמר דלאו מיניה, דבהא לא מכשיר ר"ג, כיון דהוי ברי וברי כדאמר ברפ"ב, אלא כגון שמת או דליתיה קמן דלישייליה. והא דחשיב ליה בסמוך דיעבד — לפי שלא היה יכול הולד להינשא לבת ישראל, ואפילו לממזרת אסור, דמדאורייתא כשר הוא; דהאי הוי כדיעבד, הלכה כר"ג]: (מן ד"ה ההוא ארוס ע"כ היה חסר מהתוספות):
Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:1:2.english: First, he concedes - We could explain that [the Gemara] is speaking with respect to forbidding her to the betrothed [husband], and this is its explanation: "First, he concedes," therefore she is not forbidden to him; "and furthermore, didn't Rav Yehuda etc." — it is not saying "and furthermore, even if he does not concede," for if he does not concede, it is obvious that she is forbidden to him, rather it means to say: even where there is not the reason that he concedes — such as according to Abaye at the end of the chapter [entitled] Almanah, [who holds that] since she made herself available to her betrothed, she also made herself available to the world [at large] — even so, she is not forbidden to him because she is deemed credible in accordance with Rabban Gamliel. So Rabbi Yitzchak explained to us. However, it is impossible to uphold it [this explanation], for according to his words, if so, that which Abaye said, "since she made herself available," refers to a case where they did not examine her mother; and this is not [correct], for [Abaye's statement] refers to the dispute between Rav and Shmuel, who establish in Kiddushin: What is a shetuki? One whose mother is examined [beduki]. And according to what we read in Kiddushin, "a betrothed woman who became pregnant," there is no difficulty at all. Therefore, it is necessary to explain that here [the Gemara] is not speaking of forbidding her to him, rather regarding rendering the child fit [of valid lineage]. And now "and furthermore" is according to its plain meaning: and furthermore, even if he does not concede — and not that he says it is not from him, for in that case Rabban Gamliel does not render [the child] fit, since it is a [conflict of] certain [claim] against certain [claim], as [the Gemara] states at the beginning of the second chapter — rather, such as where he died or is not before us to ask him. And that which [the Gemara] considers it immediately below [to be a case of] bedi'avad [after the fact], is because the child would not be able to marry the daughter of an Israelite, and even to a mamzeret he is forbidden, since by Torah law he is fit; [thus] since this is like bedi'avad, the halakha is in accordance with Rabban Gamliel]: (From the dibbur hamatchil "A certain betrothed man" until here was missing from the Tosafot.):

Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:4:1.hebrew: אלמנת עיסה - פירש בקונטרס שני פירושין, ושניהם דחוקים; דהא אמרינן לקמן: "איזו היא אלמנת עיסה? כל שנטמע בה ספק חלל", ומה טימוע שייך במה שנישאת לספק חלל? ועוד, דאין לשון "עיסה" נופל על אדם אחד, אלא על משפחה שייך לשון "עיסה", כדאמרינן (קדושין דף סט:): "כל הארצות עיסה לארץ ישראל, וא"י עיסה לבבל". ובתוספתא תניא: "מפני מה אמרו עיסה פסולה? מפני ספיקי חללין", ומה ספיקי חללין שייך לאלו הפירושין? ונראה לר"י ולריב"א, ד"עיסה" קורא המשפחה שנטמע בהם ספק חלל אחד או הרבה ספיקי חללים, ולהכי חשיב ליה לקמן ספק ספיקא, דכל אחד מבני המשפחה ספק אם הוא אותו ספק שנתערב בהן, אם לאו. ולקמן גרסינן: "איזהו עיסה? כל שנטמע בה כו'", ולא גרסינן "אלמנת", והכי איתא בירושלמי; ואפילו גרסינן "אלמנת", "כל שנטמע בה" קאי אעיסה. ואם תאמר: דבפרק עשרה יוחסין (קידושין דף עה.) משמע דאפילו מאן דמכשר אלמנת עיסה מודה בבת דפסולה — גבי הא דאמר רב חסדא: "הכל מודים באלמנת עיסה שפסולה לכהונה כו'", ולאפוקי מהני תנאי דתנן: "העיד רבי יהושע כו'" — ומה לי אלמנה, מה לי בת? דבת נמי הוי ספק ספיקא כמו באלמנה! וי"ל, דבת העיסה אין לה חזקה דכשרות, ואע"ג דבעלמא מקילין בספק ספיקא, הכא מעלה עשו ביוחסין, כי היכי דמצריך לקמן תרי רובי להכשיר, אף על גב דבעלמא סגי בחד רובא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:4:1.english: Almanat issa [the widow of a family of questionable lineage] - Rashi explained two interpretations, and both of them are forced: for we say below, "What is an almanat issa? Anyone into which a doubtful chalal [a disqualified priest] has been assimilated" — and what "assimilation" is relevant to the fact that she married a doubtful chalal? Moreover, the term issa [lit. "dough," i.e., a mixture] does not apply to a single person; rather, the term issa applies to a family, as we say (Kiddushin 69b): "All lands are issa relative to the Land of Israel, and the Land of Israel is issa relative to Babylonia." And in the Tosefta it is taught: "Why did they say an issa is disqualified? Because of doubtful chalalim" — and what "doubtful chalalim" [in the plural] are relevant to those interpretations? And it appears to Ri and Riva that [the Gemara] calls the family into which one doubtful chalal or many doubtful chalalim have been assimilated an "issa," and therefore [the Gemara] below considers it a double doubt [sefek sefeika], since for each member of the family there is a doubt whether he is that doubtful [individual] who became mixed among them or not. And below we read [the text as]: "What is an issa? Anyone into which [a doubtful chalal] has been assimilated, etc.," and we do not read "almanat [widow of]," and so it appears in the Jerusalem Talmud; and even if we do read "almanat," [the phrase] "into which ... has been assimilated" refers back to "issa." And if you ask: in the chapter Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 75a) it is implied that even the one who permits an almanat issa agrees regarding a daughter [of an issa] that she is disqualified — in connection with that which Rav Chisda said: "Everyone agrees regarding an almanat issa that she is disqualified from the priesthood, etc.," [which comes] to exclude these Tannaim, as we learned: "Rabbi Yehoshua testified, etc." — [so] what is the difference between a widow and a daughter, since a daughter is also a double doubt just like a widow? One can answer that the daughter of an issa does not have a presumptive status [chazakah] of fitness; and even though elsewhere we are lenient in a case of a double doubt, here they instituted a higher standard in matters of lineage, just as [the Gemara] below requires two majorities to permit [her], even though elsewhere one majority suffices.

Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:6:1.hebrew: דרבי יהושע אדר"י לא קשיא - והשתא לא מצי לשנויי דבודקת ונישאת כדמשני לעיל, כיון דהשתא אוקימנא באומרת שמא:
Tosafot on Ketubot 14a:6:1.english: [That] of Rabbi Yehoshua against [that of] Rabbi Yehoshua is not difficult - And now [the Gemara] cannot answer that she investigates and marries, as it answered above, since now we have established [the Mishnah] as [referring to a case where] she says "perhaps."
